tour.overview:
The ancient Greeks believed Delphi was the centre of the world: Zeus released two eagles from the ends of the earth, and they met here. For more than a thousand years, kings, cities and ordinary people climbed to the sanctuary of Apollo on the slopes of Mount Parnassus to put their questions to the Pythia, the priestess who spoke the god's answers in a trance. Their gifts filled the sanctuary with treasuries, statues and temples. Delphi has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

This private day takes you there from Athens through the plains of Boeotia and up into the mountains, with a licensed archaeologist guide. You walk up the Sacred Way to the Temple of Apollo, the theatre and the stadium, see the treasures found here in the Delphi Museum, visit the Tholos below the road, and have lunch in Arachova, a village of stone houses above the olive groves that run down to the sea.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Athens
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 5 km, with a steady climb up the sanctuary to the stadium

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Sanctuary of Apollo: the Sacred Way, the Treasury of the Athenians, the Temple of Apollo, the theatre and the stadium.
• The Delphi Museum.
• The Castalian Spring.
• The Sanctuary of Athena Pronaia and the Tholos.
• Arachova.

WHY THIS WORKS
We leave Athens early to climb the sanctuary in the cool of the morning and visit the museum when the sun is high, then have a relaxed lunch in the mountains.

WHO IT SUITS
History and mythology lovers, students and anyone who wants to see one of the most beautiful ancient sites in a dramatic mountain setting.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day, choose our Cape Sounion tour; if you want to continue north, combine Delphi with Meteora on a two-day trip.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about 2 hours 30 minutes each way. The upper sanctuary is steep and exposed: wear good shoes and a hat. In winter Arachova is a ski village and the road can be snowy.

days.name: The Sanctuary of Apollo, the Delphi Museum, the Tholos of Athena Pronaia and lunch in Arachova
days.description:
What to expect: the oracle of Apollo and its mountain setting, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 7:00 for the drive north-west, through the plains of Boeotia past Thebes and up into the foothills of Mount Parnassus, with a coffee stop on the way. You arrive at about 9:30 and meet your guide at the entrance.

You walk up the Sacred Way, which zigzags up the hillside between the foundations of the treasuries where Greek cities displayed their offerings. The Treasury of the Athenians, rebuilt from its original marble blocks, was paid for with spoils from the battle of Marathon in 490 BC. You pass the Rock of the Sibyl and the Athenian Stoa and reach the Temple of Apollo, where the Pythia sat on her tripod above a chasm and answered questions, and where the maxims 'Know thyself' and 'Nothing in excess' were carved. Above the temple, the theatre, with 35 rows of seats for some 5,000 spectators, looks across the valley of the Pleistos, and higher still the stadium, the best-preserved in Greece, hosted the Pythian Games every four years.

In the Delphi Museum you see the treasures found in the sanctuary: the bronze Charioteer, cast around 474 BC to celebrate a chariot victory, with his eyes of glass and stone still in place; the Sphinx of the Naxians; the omphalos, the stone 'navel of the world'; and the sculptures of the Siphnian Treasury. You then stop at the Castalian Spring, where pilgrims purified themselves, and walk down to the Sanctuary of Athena Pronaia to see the Tholos, an elegant round temple of the 4th century BC whose three restored columns are the most photographed image of Delphi.

Lunch is in Arachova, a mountain village of stone houses and cobbled lanes ten minutes away, known for its woven rugs, formaela cheese and red wine. You drive back to Athens in the afternoon, arriving at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Athens.
09:30 – Sanctuary of Apollo (about 2 hours).
11:30 – Delphi Museum (about 1 hour).
12:45 – Castalian Spring and the Tholos of Athena Pronaia.
13:30 – Lunch in Arachova.
15:00 – Drive back to Athens.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The sanctuary closes early in winter; we adapt the timing.
• The stadium may be closed in bad weather or for conservation.
• Delphi can be combined with Meteora on a two-day trip with a night in Kalambaka.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 2 hours 30 minutes each way, on good roads with a coffee stop. The scenery in the mountains is beautiful.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the archaeological site and the Delphi Museum. The Tholos area is included in the same ticket.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km, with a steady climb up the Sacred Way to the stadium on uneven stone. You can stop at the temple or the theatre if you prefer.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch in Arachova. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the story of the oracle, the stadium race and the Charioteer. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The museum is accessible, but the sanctuary is a steep hillside with steps and uneven paths. You can see the Tholos and the lower sanctuary more easily.

faq.question: Can we combine Delphi and Meteora?
faq.answer: Yes, on a two-day trip with a night in Kalambaka. Doing both in one day from Athens is too long to enjoy.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops. Arachova's shops are optional browsing.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Shoes with grip, a hat and sun cream in summer, and warm layers in winter: Delphi is 570 metres above sea level.

faq.question: Is it cold in winter?
faq.answer: It can be cold and occasionally snowy, especially in Arachova at almost 1,000 metres. The site is often wonderfully clear and quiet.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to November. Summer is hot on the exposed slopes; we start early.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
